anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services
Management Advice and Related Consulting Services

merger_description:
Roma BidCo Pty Ltd (**Roma Bidco**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of Bio101 Financial Advisory Pty Ltd (**Bio101**) by way of a share sale agreement (the **Acquisition**).

Roma BidCo is a special purpose acquisition vehicle which is majority owned by Pemba Capital Fund III, L.P. (**Pemba Fund III**), a private equity fund managed by Pemba Capital Partners Pty Ltd (**Pemba**).

Pemba is an investor in high-growth and entrepreneurial businesses, with over AUD 2 billion in assets under management. Pemba has interests across various sectors, including business services, education & training, financial services, healthcare, and technology. One of Pemba’s portfolio companies (also within the Pemba Fund III) is Stannards Accountants & Advisors Pty Ltd (**Stannards**), an accounting and business advisory services provider, headquartered in Melbourne.

Bio101 is a Melbourne-based accounting and advisory firm that services clients in the healthcare, biotech and life sciences sector. Bio101’s services include company secretarial services, transaction advisory, bookkeeping services, and outsourced CFO and finance-function support.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is limited horizontal overlap between Pemba and
Bio101 in the supply of accounting and business advisory
services in Australia, with the parties focussing on different
customers and market segments
b. the parties’ combined share of supply of accounting and
business advisory services in Victoria and nationally is
estimated to be low and the increment arising from the
Acquisition is expected to be small
c. there are alternative providers of accounting and business
advisory services available to customers in Victoria and
nationally, including with a focus on the healthcare, biotech
and life sciences sector.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
